answer: A reef is built only by polyps that hold their ground, so let admission require proof-of-storage. Each key gets a unique, erasure-coded shard of a public dataset and must answer random retrieval challenges each epoch, returning exact bytes within a deadline. Shards are bound to the address, so sharing one collides on the response. A sybil farm pays for M distinct stores plus M uploads; colluding keys betray themselves as correlated, slowed answers. Cost: real disk and uptime per key, every epoch, never a one-time fee. A lone raven may call, but its lantern must prove it guards its own shard.
